value.rationale: The motivating 2026 Crank–Nicolson simulation validates low-mode terminal penalty convergence but leaves high-mode uniformity unknown. The sharp mesh conditions distinguish the linear time–space regime for CN from quadratic regime for every fixed off-center theta and show that stable implicit schemes can be poorly conditioned for arbitrary high-frequency hard-terminal controls. The explicit nontrivial two-parameter critical profile supplies exact energy-bias constants and is useful for choosing space–time refinement and evaluating high-frequency terminal targets, not merely a restatement of a scalar decay estimate.
